content.comment_body: Hello, does anyone know if [product_name] [article_no] has issues with the up/down counter feature? We developed an application for a two-channel encoder on [product_name] [article_no] and it worked well, but it seems not to function with [product_name] [version_no]. The setup is straightforward: Channel A goes to input I5 (connected to Cnt) and Channel B to input I6 (connected to Dir). In [product_name] [version_no], counting up and down works as expected based on the encoder direction. However, with [product_name] [version_no], the counter sometimes resets or the displayed count is unexpectedly low. Slow encoder movements read fine; with faster movements, counts become erratic. The device is a 12/24RCE and the encoder speed is below 4 Hz.
I haven't experienced such problems with [product_name] [article_no]. Which exact type (Standard or FS04) is it and what firmware version does your [product_name] have?
Could you please share your [product_name] program so it can be reviewed?
It's the latest [product_name] [version_no]. Where is the program? I also have the new version and haven't had counter problems. You'll need to zip the program to attach it.
Hi, the program is pretty simple. I've attached it for reference.
I transferred your program to my [product_name] and it works: the counter moves forward and backward, and reset functions correctly. I don't have an actual encoder to fully test it, though.

It's worth noting that this program was developed and works in [product_name] [article_no]; the wiring and encoder are unchanged, but it doesn't function properly with [product_name] [article_no]. Videos are attached for reference. Using a 25 PPR encoder, slow movements result in correct counting, but at higher speeds, the counter behaves unpredictably. For example, in the SLOW_SPEED video, the encoder is turned slowly up to a count of 125 and then reversed with correct counts. In the FAST_SPEED video, moving the encoder quickly causes the count to, for instance, decrease from 80 to 64 or jump unexpectedly. The encoder and cables are shielded, and pulse frequency remains below 4 Hz.

Can anyone else test the counter functionality? With [product_name] [article_no], the counter works well with the encoder; with [product_name] [article_no] and firmware [version_no], it doesn't function properly. Any advice would be appreciated.

Hello, has anyone solved the encoder problem yet? In the latest version, is connecting channel A to cnt and channel B to dir sufficient for proper operation? Can anyone confirm this? I can't locate an example of this configuration. Some sources claim it's not possible to connect a direction encoder.
Reliable A/B encoder evaluation isn't feasible. [product_name] isn't designed for this type of use.

That's disappointing. I expected encoder support to be built-in. Typically, the A and B signals are offset so the direction can be determined by state transitions. The question is how quickly the DIR input can be read in the program.

That's a misconception. [product_name] can't handle this properly. Pulse counting happens outside the program cycle, but direction changes only occur within a single cycle, causing inconsistent histories when counting.

analysis.insight_summary: A user reports that the up/down counter feature in [product_name] [version_no] (especially with firmware [version_no] and article [article_no]) isn’t reliably tracking counts from a two-channel encoder at increased speeds. The identical setup and program worked fine in the earlier [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]), but in the newer unit, the counter sometimes resets or displays lower-than-expected values. Other participants haven't encountered this issue but haven't run real encoder tests, so reproducibility remains unclear.
analysis.user_expectations: The user would like [product_name] [version_no] to reliably perform up/down counting from a two-channel encoder, matching the stability and accuracy of the previous [version_no], without missed pulses, resets, or erratic counts—even at moderate encoder speeds.
